about: Who keeps each service (#9895). A town draws one person per service from its list by its stable identity. A portrait is the keeper's bust in the dialogue: a rig-c parts rig the Engine poses live in the dialogue frame's window (#10027, made with the parts-rig route in art/people/README.md), its resting clip and the clip it plays while a new line is said, its texel (rig units a texel) and frame [x, y, side]: the square of the rig's plane the window shows, in rig units, whole texels from its origin. A person without one shows no portrait. A figure is the keeper standing at their door in the town view: a rig-c parts rig the Engine poses at runtime, its looping clip, metres per rig unit, pixelGrid (the Engine draws it smooth and lit, then cuts it into blocks of this many screen pixels on one grid anchored at its feet, rusty-engine #10716) and poseRate (poses a second its clip steps at: 8, as the baked figures played, so fewer blocks change a frame; it divides the loop), and optionally palette (a file of sRGB hex colours each block takes the nearest of once lit, made by art/people/palette.py; none keeps the blocks' own colours); the kit piece's keeper spot is where they stand.
